A1.justification: Both PDFs, including their appendices, are readable and describe the same DG–CA3 navigation agent. Matching equations, experiments and results support comparison despite the changed title and presentation.

before.justification: v1 reports original navigation simulations, architecture comparisons, neural representation analyses and decoder-weight perturbation results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds noise experiments, repetition-parameter sweeps and quantitative place-field analyses.

M1.justification: The architecture, sequence dynamics and loss equation remain unchanged. However, the reported advantage estimator changes from GAE with lambda 0.95 in v1 Sections 6.3–6.4 to V-trace returns in v3 Appendix B.4. This revises the specified training procedure; the PDFs do not establish whether implementation changed or the description was corrected.

E1.justification: v3 adds navigation with Gaussian-corrupted visual inputs (Figure A5), introducing a new sensory condition within the existing maze task. The environment family, goal-transfer scenarios, additional maps and encoder variants were already covered in v1.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator set remains Random RNN, HiPPO-LegS, HiPPO-LegT, HiPPO-LagT and LSTM. The new noise experiment uses the existing dense LSTM comparator; newly cited navigation models are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends the evaluation design with an R=1–32 sweep at two frame skips, noise levels 0–80, and success summaries at 150M and 100M frames respectively. It also introduces place-field entropy and center-of-mass shift measurements. These additions accompany the reported GAE-to-V-trace revision; the original main comparison protocol is otherwise retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test repetition sensitivity across movement speeds (Figure A1), robustness to visual noise (Figure A5), place-field broadening along sequences (Figure 5B), and single-unit stabilization and remapping (Figure A10). These substantially extend v1's existing sequence-length, encoder, map and training-parameter controls.

E5.justification: Main learning curves retain mean and standard-error reporting over six seeds, while the implementation appendix retains the same five named seeds. Added experiments reuse that seed list and existing reporting practices. No increased repeat count, significance testing or confidence-interval procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 is numerically unchanged, but v3 adds substantial results for repetition sensitivity, noise robustness, entropy and remapping. For example, Table A4 reports success at 100M frames and noise sigma 80 of 0.477±0.072 for DG+CA3 versus 0.373±0.008 for dense LSTM. These are additional condition-specific results, not improvements to the retained Table 1 scores.

T1.justification: The sequence equations, loss formula and spatial-information definition are retained. Appendix B.2 expands the existing Kronecker representation into equivalent block matrices and explains their interpretation; it introduces no new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: sparse inputs and intrinsic sequences support navigation and hippocampus-like representations, with an advantage over LSTM under sparse but not dense input. The new experiments support these claims without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: v3 expands interpretation of R as a temporal-smoothing prior with a timing-precision tradeoff and connects noise experiments to the proposed reliance on strong sensory cues. It adds entorhinal-pathway interpretations, distinctions from successor representations, and applicability to sequences without prominent theta oscillations. The explicit limitations appendix is essentially retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository pointer and specifies noise magnitudes and pixel-intensity units for the new experiments. It also revises training-estimator documentation and condenses implementation descriptions, dropping details such as camera height, field of view and the 120-second checkpoint interval. Most architecture and training hyperparameters remain documented.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning relative to circuit-constrained neuroscience, successor representations and navigation models using allocentric or spatially informative inputs. New discussion includes Kumar et al. and Vijayabaskaran and Cheng. It also newly labels the retained population-vector analysis as novel and connects it to representational-similarity literature.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title and author presentation, rewrites portions of the introduction and discussion, expands the matrix explanation, and condenses training configuration into labeled paragraphs. Appendix organization and captions are revised, while the main Methods/Results sequence and substantial prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 merges and redraws the original conceptual and architecture figures, places existing LSTM analyses beside CA3 results, and consolidates correlation and spatial-information plots with the new entropy panel. New supplementary tables and figures accompany extensive changes to legends, captions, figure composition and conference layout.

improvement.justification: The new noise and repetition controls, entropy analysis and remapping measurements strengthen empirical support for interpretations that were less directly tested in v1. Side-by-side comparisons and a code pointer also improve assessability. Gains are limited by unchanged core results, omitted implementation details and the unreconciled GAE-to-V-trace revision.
